findings.summary: _flux_at re-implements the capability scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:268 _point_flux already owns (a RegularGridInterpolator over the same (radius, height) map, documented as 'genuine bilinear interpolation of the map at arbitrary points'), so the same sampling now exists twice in the prototype tree with divergent edge behaviour: _flux_at silently clamps an out-of-grid point to the last cell and extrapolates, where _point_flux returns nan.

The caption calls the pale blue contours 'the shared levels inside the wall' after identifying the solid dark stepped outline as 'the physical DIII-D first wall', but render.py:131 computes the levels inside the registered pseudo-wall and the drawn contours extend outside the physical wall on both panels, so the levels the caption names are inside the dotted reference rectangle, not the wall.

_corpus_row reads the parquet corpus under bench.DEFAULT_DATA and imports the whole benchmark (and its jax dependency) to obtain the EFIT boundary and lower null, so the committed SVG cannot be regenerated from the committed receipts and evidence alone; storing the boundary in the arm npz at solve time would keep the render path reading only its own records.
